title: Quasi-coherence from the affine annihilator image
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $J$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaf data of finite type [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and $F$ a quasi-coherent module sheaf [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $G$ be a module sheaf and $\iota:G\to F$ a monomorphism. Assume that for every affine open $U$, the image of $\iota(U)$ consists exactly of the sections $s$ killed by every $a\in J(U)$. Then $G$ is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: Realize J.toModules as the kernel of the structure-module map to the closed-subscheme pushforward. The source-library closed-immersion pushforward theorem and kernel theorem prove its quasi-coherence. Pull finite local generators back to the slice over an affine W, reusing Scheme.Modules.isFiniteType_over from FinitePushforwardCoherent through a proof-only import all. The affine finite-type criterion then gives finitely many spanning sections e_j of J.toModules(W); their images g_j generate the ideal J(W). Only the quasi-coherent pushforward clause of the bundled closed-immersion node is used, with no Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: Given s in G(D(f)), quasi-coherence of F gives t in F(W) restricting to f^n iota(s). Each restricted g_j belongs to J(D(f)), so the assumed image formula makes the restriction of g_j t zero. The affine localization equality criterion gives exponents d_j killing g_j t. Let D be the finite supremum of the d_j (zero for the empty family). Then every g_j kills f^D t. A kernel-and-span argument on J.toModules(W) shows that every a in J(W) kills f^D t. The image formula on W lifts this numerator to v in G(W). Naturality and sectionwise injectivity of iota give v restricted to D(f) = f^(D+n) s.

source.place: Properties, Tag 01PO (lemma-sections-annihilated-by-ideal), proof; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01PO

proof.text: If t in G(W) restricts to zero on D(f), its image in F(W) also does. The affine localization equality criterion in F gives n with f^n iota(t)=0. Sectionwise injectivity of iota gives f^n t=0. Together with the preceding lifting condition, apply the proved principal-open criterion for quasi-coherence; it supplies the tilde identification and affine-cover gluing.

theorem annihilator_subsheaf_quasicoherent (X : Scheme.{u}) (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    [J.toModules.IsFiniteType] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (G : X.Modules) (ι : G ⟶ F) [Mono ι]
    (himage : ∀ (U : X.affineOpens) (s : Γ(F, U.1)),
      s ∈ Set.range (ι.app U.1) ↔ ∀ a ∈ J.ideal U, a • s = 0) :
    G.IsQuasicoherent
